Review Cal.com?

Reviewers mostly see Cal.com as a polished, easy scheduling tool with a clean interface, smooth setup, and strong calendar integrations, especially for Google and Microsoft users. Many say it feels better than Calendly, with useful customization, embedding, reminders, payments, and even built-in video. Technical users also value self-hosting and the open API; makers of IFTTT and Slashy specifically praise its flexibility and developer experience. The main complaints are uneven support, some Microsoft/Exchange connection gaps, and confusion over which features are truly open source.

Used Cal for a bit now, and I prefer the easy to schedule as well as integration with M365 and other apps. The landing page to schedule a meeting is no jazz, simple and does the job. The backend setting allows users to customise with third party app developers and integrate the scheduling, payment with Stripe and workspace with either Google or Microsoft, all comes together. Very few or none out there on the product market are at par with Cal.com. Can't wait for Cal.ai to be in hands for general availability.

A Game Changer for Scheduling I've been using various scheduling applications over the years, but CAL has completely revolutionized my experience. The user interface is clean, intuitive, and visually appealing. It's incredibly easy to manage multiple calendars, set reminders, and coordinate meetings across different time zones. The app's seamless integration with other platforms like Google Calendar and Outlook is just the cherry on top. This is a must-have tool for anyone looking to stay organized and efficient. 5/5 stars, hands down because of its inbuilt video conferencing tool called as Cal Video.
